newsitem.title: USA: Fireworks due this week in IPO market turnaround.
newsitem.headline: Fireworks due this week in IPO market turnaround.

text.p: Initial public offerings could recapture their lost status as Wall Street darlings this week as institutional investors crowd back into the IPO market and pump up opening-day premiums.

"We put a calendar together and Holy Mother of Pearl -- It just exploded," said John Fitzgibbon, editor of the IPO Aftermarket. Over 40 companies are scheduled to go public and almost a quarter could fetch stiff premiums, analysts say.

The IPO Value Monitor's director of research Ryan Jacob said, "It has all the ingredients: The pipeline has filled up, the broader market is doing well with the Dow hitting new highs, and we have lots of big names on deals to focus a lot of attention on the IPO market."

Spanish-language TV broadcaster Univision Communications Corp., sunglasses maker Gargoyles Inc., Ocwen Financial, marketer Snyder Communications, and temporary staffing agency StaffMark Inc. are just of few of the deals expected to surge this week.

Early demand for IPOs dropped off sharply in July after a broader market slump, exacerbated by the seasonal slowdown. Many companies did grow and post gains in their first few weeks or months, but opening day surges have been scarce.

But the super-hot opening last week of International Network Services shocked many market players out of their summer lethargy. The stock nearly doubled, providing the first clue the market has turned the corner.
On Friday, International Network stock gained 50 cents on Nasdaq to $31.25 vs. its initial price of $16 in its debut Wednesday.

"It's the starting gun for the latest IPO craze ... There were no extraordinary circumstances surrounding that deal so it shows a certain confidence has returned to the market. The institutional investors are (now) willing to pay for higher valuations on stocks," Jacob said.

The renewed interest in technology stocks is also helping IPOs, analysts said. The technology-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index, now at 1,219.69, is closing in fast on its all-time record high of 1,249.15 set June 5.
Univision's $150 million offering should be a star this week, analysts say.
"This is one of the best deals of the week," said Manish Shah, editor of the IPO Maven.

Potential investors packed a presentation at a New York Hotel hoping to learn more about the company, he said, and Univision has "a strong gang of big-name underwriters," including Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette, Goldman Sachs, Merrill Lynch and Morgan Stanley.

Other offerings that could also fetch premiums are Lehman's three deals: Navigation Technologies Corp., Tri-Point Medical and Cox Radio; and Smith Barney's American Residential Services, Gargoyles, and Integrated Living Communities Inc.
Another hot deal is Merrill Lynch's Rockshox Inc., which makes suspension systems for mountain bikes. The company is offering 4.8 million shares for $13 to $15 each.

"It's not cheap," said Shah, "but the young founders of the company have really cornered the high end of the market. If they can go global and broaden to the lower ends, this stock could do really well in the longer term."

Other deals that Fitzgibbon says could surge are Lightbridge by Cowen & Co., Cellnet Data by Morgan Stanley, Abacus Direct, Coffee People Inc., LCC International, Leap Group, and Peerless Systems Inc.

A sharp hike in interest rates at Tuesday's Federal Reserve meeting, if it were to hurt the broader market, might be the only thing that could slow the accerating IPO train, analysts say, but for now the market may be shaping up to beat its own records.
"We're going to see more filings and deals opening up with those types of premiums and it's very possible," said Jacob. "But it will be a tough bogey to beat last spring."
